newsitem.title: USA: Texaco Inc raises earnings goals.
newsitem.headline: Texaco Inc raises earnings goals.

text.p: Texaco Inc raised its earnings goals to more than $2 billion by the turn of the century, and increased other operating targets, based on this year's operating performance and expected strong performance through the end of the decade, Chief Executive Peter Bijur said Wednesday.

Addressing some 200 security analysts at Texaco headquarters here, Bijur cited improvements reflected in the company's year-to-date results, including nine-month earnings that have surpassed full-year 1995 results, an increase in the quarterly dividend and a reduced debt-to-capital ratio.
"To sum it up," he said, "our operating performance this year has simply been terrific and has exceeded most expectations."
Among the new targets set, Texaco will strive to double 1995 earnings of $1.152 billion to more than $2 billion by the turn of the century.
Vice President Patrick Lynch noted that the company's previous target had been to double 1994 earnings before 2000, adding that this has almost been accomplished in 1996.

Bijur said the company will do this while maintaining a debt to capital ratio of 35 percent to 40 percent. He also said the company will increase production over the next five years by more than 50 percent from 1996 levels to a total of some 1.7 million barrels of oil equivalent per day by 2001.

Bijur said the settlement last month of a civil rights suit will have no impact on fourth quarter results, explaining that the company has adequate reserves to make the $115 million payment. He also said that payment will have no impact on the company's capital spending in 1996 and beyond.
In addition to the payment, he said, Texaco is making a one-time increase in the pay of African-American employees at a cost of about $400 million.

Lynch said each $1 per barrel increase in the average worldwide price of oil adds $141 million to Texaco's annual net income, while each $0.10 per thousand cubic feet increase in natural gas prices adds $65 million.
Bijur said the company's 1997 planning is based on an expectation that West Texas Intermediate oil prices will average at least $19.50 per barrel and U. S. natural gas prices at $1.90 per cubic feet.
This compares to 1996's planning assumptions of $18 per barrel and $1.75 per thousand cubic feet, he noted.
For 1998, he added, Texaco planning is based on a 1.5 percent per year increase in oil prices and flat natural gas prices.

Lynch pointed out that the company has decreased its cash expenses per barrel of oil produced to $4.84 per barrel this year from $5.55 in 1993, adding the company expects this to decline to $4.78 in 1997.
He said the company is projecting a debt to equity ratio of 34.4 percent next year, compared to this year's 34.0 percent.
